rationale: The live batch path exits 0 on success and routes SQL-like failures through MiniDbError::exit_code to 1, IO/storage/WAL failures to 3, while clap Args::parse handles CLI usage failures with exit code 2.

run_with_io keeps separate stdout and stderr writers; render_result writes query data to stdout, writes per-statement summaries to stderr, and suppresses those summaries when quiet is set. Writing the summary to stdout as in option D is inconsistent.

Session::open invokes replay_wal on startup. The WAL reader follows the append-only record stream, and collect_committed_ops replays only operations whose transaction has a Commit record, excluding the uncommitted suffix.
The live CLI parser passes the --format value to OutputFormat::parse; yaml becomes MiniDbError::Cli, and run prints the message to stderr and returns exit code 2 before evaluating SQL.
main exits 0 when cli::run succeeds and otherwise uses MiniDbError::exit_code: Usage maps to 2, parse/type/SQL to 1, and IO/storage/serialization to 3.

The executor defines distinct SeqScan and IndexScan structs plus separate Filter, Project, NestedLoopJoin, Sort, Limit, Insert, Update, and Delete types. The reachable planner constructs SeqScan or IndexScan directly; there is no fused ScanKind operator, making option B inconsistent.

Cli::run_sql sends result data through emit_output to stdout and, unless quiet, sends the summary through emit_summary using eprintln. JSON rendering emits only the JSON value on stdout, so option D violates the reachable routing behavior.

run_inner reaches Storage::open at startup. Storage reads the WAL, committed_prefix retains only complete Begin-to-Commit transactions and drops rolled-back or unterminated records, then applies the committed statements to the database image.

The reachable DML path calls auto_begin, whose call to begin sets auto_commit=false; the subsequent auto_commit checks that flag and therefore does not commit, leaving the transaction active. DDL bypasses this wrapping entirely, and no canonical option fully describes the resulting mixed and apparently buggy durability behavior.

run_inner invokes Engine::recover_from_wal before loading the catalog. Wal::replay scans the append-only records, selects page and catalog writes only from transactions with Commit records, and Engine applies those writes before checkpointing.

The crate defines one MiniDbError enum with parse, type, storage, IO, SQL, transaction, catalog, and index variants plus a crate-wide Result alias and conversion implementations; top-level entry paths propagate this type to main.

A complete src search finds every direct eprintln! use in src/cli.rs and none in non-CLI modules. Reachable transaction, recovery, storage, and executor diagnostics outside the CLI use the log facade.
